To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NK cells from patients with DCL have a reduced response to L. mexicana LPG stimulation, which is associated with a down-regulation of TLR2, JAK/STAT, IFN-α, IL-10, IL-12 and TNF-α genes.

NK cells from DCLI patients showed a reduced expression of genes encoding proteins of the TLR and JNK/STAT signaling pathways, which are important for the NK cell response to LPG, and that the down regulation of these genes was independent of LPG.
NK cells from DML patients are functionally impaired and show down-regulated TLR and JAX/STAT signaling pathway genes.

the molecular mechanisms of NK cell dysfunction in patients with diffuse leishmaniasisis and the identification of potential therapeutic targets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DCL patients have a reduced NK-cell response to LPG, which may be associated to down-regulation of TLRs and JAK/ STAT pathway genes.
the down-regulation of TLRs and JAK/ STAT signaling pathways in NK cells from patients with DCL is associated with the NK-cell dysfunction observed in this group of patients.

the down-regulation of TLRs and JAK/ STAT signaling pathways in NK cells from patients infected with L. mexicana could be an important mechanism for the impairment of NK-cell effector functions in patients with DCLS, which could be an important factor for the development of DCL.

NK cells from DCLI patients are unable to respond to the LPG stimulus and are not capable of activating the TLR and JNK/STAT pathways, which may be related to the disease severity.
